record_notice: SOURCED RECORD — cooking facts paraphrased from McCormick Australia and temperature guidance from Health Canada, both first accessed 2026-09-14. No source text or photograph is reproduced. The final oven mode is ambiguous in the recipe source; the conventional-only path below is an explicit editorial choice. This record has not been kitchen-tested here and has had no professional food-safety review. Measure temperature and check tenderness separately.

alt: Mediterranean lamb and potato tray bake

summary: Forequarter lamb chops and thinly sliced Pontiac potatoes baked together under a sealed cover, then finished uncovered until the potatoes colour. The times apply to chops baked under potatoes with a sealed cover; use a separate recipe for uncovered, meat-only roasting.

ingredients.note: The source is a seasoning manufacturer and specifies its own branded sachet. Check the packet for allergens; this record has not verified its contents.
The source says only thinly sliced and states no thickness, so none is given here.

ingredients.quantity: 1 tablespoon, stated by the source as 20 mL
ingredients.note: This source defines its tablespoon as the 20 mL Australian spoon. A 15 mL tablespoon holds a quarter less.

method.instruction: The source starts at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan-forced. Use 200°C conventional throughout, an editorial choice because the source’s final stage does not specify a mode. Preheat on that conventional setting.
Grease a shallow baking dish large enough to hold the four chops flat in a single layer.
Season both sides of the chops with about 1 1/2 tablespoons of the recipe base and lay them in the dish.
Turn the potato slices through the olive oil with the rest of the recipe base, then arrange them over the chops.
Cover with baking paper and then foil, pinching the edges tightly to seal, and bake for 45 minutes.

Remove the cover and bake uncovered for a further 15 minutes, until the potatoes are golden brown and the lamb is tender. The source says 200°C here but gives NO oven mode; it does not establish 200°C fan-forced. Continue at 200°C conventional, as recommended in step 1. If you started on fan, switch to conventional; the source gives no final fan setting.

Measure the thickest part of each chop away from bone. Health Canada gives 63°C internal for medium-rare lamb cuts and 71°C for medium. Reaching 63°C does not establish tenderness: also check that the potatoes are cooked through and the lamb is tender. Time alone establishes neither endpoint.

yield_note: Serves 4. Source prep: 5 minutes; cook: 60 minutes (45 covered + 15 uncovered); total: about 65 minutes by editorial addition, excluding preheating and any extra cooking needed. Equipment: conventional oven, shallow baking dish holding the chops in one layer, baking paper and foil suitable for that oven setting, knife, board and probe thermometer. No resting time is supplied by the source.

provenance_note: Recipe facts paraphrased from McCormick Australia, first accessed 2026-09-14; temperature guidance is Health Canada's. The recipe uses a branded seasoning sachet and Pontiac potatoes. It gives no chop weight or thickness, no potato-slice thickness and no added liquid. Its final 200°C has no mode: the conventional-only path is an editorial resolution, not a newly verified source instruction or a fan conversion. The sealed baking-paper-and-foil cover and potatoes are part of this method; do not transfer its times to uncovered, meat-only cooking or derive a time from a 500 g pack. Thickness, cover, potato preparation and appliance behaviour matter. Check the material manufacturers' heat limits.

caveats: Forequarter chops are shoulder chops, not a rack or a whole shoulder roast. Their thickness is unspecified; the sealed cover and potato layer are essential context for these timings. A pack weight is not a timing rule, and a measured safety endpoint is not proof of tenderness.
Health Canada gives 63°C internal for a medium-rare lamb cut and 71°C for medium. Measure at the thickest point away from the bone; bone conducts heat and reads high.
Raw lamb juices run in the dish. Wash hands, board and knife after handling, and keep the raw packaging away from the sliced potatoes.
The branded seasoning sachet has not been checked for allergens by this project; read its packet.
This record has had no professional food-safety review and has not been kitchen-tested by this project.
